diffs.diff: pin count: part has 12 (VIN 3V3 GND SCL SDA CS SAO OCS INT2 INT1 SCX SDX), datasheet reading has 11 (VIN 3V3 GND SCL SDA CS SAO / OCS INT2 INT1 SCX SDX)
diffs.evidence: The GY-BMI160 silkscreen photo in hanyazou/BMI160-Arduino files/wiring3.png shows 12 separate pads: VIN, 3V3, GND, SCL, SDA, CS and SAO on one edge, and OCS, INT2, INT1, SCX and SDX on the other. SAO and OCS are different pins on different edges. In issue #2 the GY-BMI160 labels are listed separately ('SAO and SDX and OCS'), and a continuity test maps them as 'SAO -> SDO (MISO), CS -> CSB, SDA -> SDx, SCL -> SCx'. OCS goes to the chip's OCSB, pin 10 in the Bosch BMI160 datasheet pinout. The second reading wrongly merged 'SAO / OCS' into one pin.
